title: An exact classical threshold in the binary triangle network

comparators.scope: 25 explicit fixed contracts including the full arbitrary-measurable-model theorem, all eight output probabilities in Corollary2, finite gap, barycentres, reduction, calculus and exact attainment; historical complete positive replay remains deferred.

comparators.rejection_detail: An extra False premise changes P15Contract.lemma_7

comparators.scope: 25-target suite with deliberate illegal proof dependency.
comparators.rejection_detail: P15Contract.illegalProof is outside the permitted axioms

main_results.scope: Every measurable independent-source TriangleModel with stochastic binary responses and M1=M3=0 satisfies M2<=tStar; exact attainment is included without finite-source or deterministic-response assumptions.
For 0<=t<=1, the actual eight-outcome p_t distribution is triangle local exactly when t<=tStar.
A bounded measurable finite-dimensional map has a barycentre represented by at most d+1 sampled values from any prescribed full-measure set, without a finite-range assumption.
One deterministic ternary maximum dominates all measurable stochastic triangle models.
Every nonexceptional ternary response table satisfies the 9/25 gap for all simplex laws, including zero source probabilities.
For positive x_i,y_i with x_i+y_i<1, constrained stationarity forces all three x_i to agree and all three y_i to agree; the supporting moment-gradient regularity is established.
